opencode.note: OpenCode v2 never auto-updates under OLYMPUS. The vendored CLI is updated only after the isolated conformance gate approves the exact version; 2.4.2 passed the full gate on 2026-11-26 (the first run hit a transient v2-session-list 503; the clean retry passed all checks).

releases.title: Cleanup and truth
highlights: Dead surfaces removed: the legacy build-talent editor, design-studio modal, MCP detail panel, plasma orb and sync-map scope module. The sync-map left-pane union, perf-route probe and stale suite list are gone with them.
Dependency pruning: nine unused devDependencies (CodeMirror, xterm, Radix tooltip) removed; npm pruned 34 packages. The runtime and build remain unchanged.

Documentation truth pass: README go-balanced roster corrected (Athena/Hermes/Dionysus/Prometheus), AGENTS.md now says v0.1.5 with 10 gods + 61 live demigods, 39 tools, 1,032 retrieval chunks and 609 resonance signatures, and the strategy comments no longer claim GLM-5.3 is Apollo.
Testing page corrected: 35 public suites and 66 total, including the v0.1.4 resonance, derived-build, RLM, embedding-cache and instinct-quarantine suites.
Gates: 8/8 hygiene, 66/66 suites, v0.1.5 UI gate, build:app. v0.1.2 remains the stable release; v0.1.4 is the test candidate.

releases.title: Resonance, derived builds, bounded RLM
highlights: Symphony Resonance Index: 8,235 historical outcomes pre-aggregated into 609 task signatures. The first pass exposed 31 fake quick circuits made of hop ids; the vocabulary rejects them and certification fixtures never gate a dispatch. The honest real count is 0 until a task class repeats; the mechanism is tested at 12 successes / 1 failure = 0.867 coherence.

Build Compiler: a hop that matches no curated build gets a derived loadout validated against real skills, registered MCPs and god-owned demigods. Derived builds are cold and recorded, never written to the catalog; promotion needs 5+ samples at 80%+ coherence plus a human click. The hop prompt now carries the real tier.

RLM Context Envelope: recursion rides the hop DAG with depth <= 2, <= 4 children per parent, child budgets <= parent and plan-time cycle rejection. The child sees the goal, parent artifacts and its slice, never the whole campaign; OLYMPUS_RLM=1 enables it and off is byte-identical.

Retrieval first-run: content-addressed embedding cache (a --force rebuild skips unchanged text), a background index job with core/all phases and real progress, and a Cost-style skeleton instead of a full-surface loader.

v0.1.2 regressions fixed: the brain no longer auto-drops haze/cloud/signals (its outline is back); LLM Strategy offline fallbacks come from the canonical table (no Apollo GLM-5.3); god-detail never opens empty.

AIME instinct audit: 190 empirical, 187 project-scoped, 1 fixture and 0 true duplicates (38 similarity candidates rejected); quarantine/restore are byte-verified and nothing was moved before the AIME test.
Gates: 8/8 hygiene, 66/66 suites, v0.1.4 UI gate, build:app. v0.1.2 remains the stable release.

releases.title: Performance and truth — 60 FPS, separate Craft/References, honest quick circuits
highlights: The atlas pauses its frame loop after 2.2s idle and wakes on the next interaction; the Pantheon measures 60 FPS p50/p95 with no long tasks in the real Electron software window. v0.1.4 removed the silent auto-lean: the user preset is the only quality switch, so the brain keeps its full silhouette.

Craft and References are separate menus. Craft keeps ArtCraft and the 13 vendored apps, and detects/launches Blender, Godot, OBS, Inkscape, Krita, DaVinci Resolve and Shotcut in the active project with fixed args and no shell string.

References is its own library. Use stages an editable Apollo prompt that asks HOW to use the reference (page/section, keep/adapt/recreate, constraints) and never sends automatically. New free/open-source sources: ReactBits (MIT + Commons Clause), Motion Primitives (MIT), Kokonut UI (MIT).

Callimachus now runs a deterministic 15-minute pass and spends a model pass at most once per hour, only for cross-project evidence. The confidence heuristic's 33 fake quick circuits are archived; the honest census is 0 validated, 187 project-scoped and 55 technical. God Intelligence shows last/next pass and the budget.
Cost paints the last measured GO usage and forecast before the console sync; the hourly chart is never a skeleton. Sync Map was removed (stale, no unique purpose).
OLYMPUS describes itself as a multi-agent AI workspace — not an operating system — in the app metadata, package, installer, README and architecture docs.
Fourteen current screens, one per menu, including the fully loaded Cost chart; README and UX-TOUR updated.

releases.title: Fluidity — one Apollo terminal, clean Parthenon, quick circuits
highlights: Marks go to ONE place: Apollo in the terminal. The parallel god chats/inbox modal are deleted; a batch is formatted once and drained as a visible HIGH queue item. Apollo asks up to three questions with 2–4 concrete options when the intent is ambiguous.

The Parthenon is clean: no status-brief card, no duplicated campaign/Atlas strips, one Ask Apollo, one primary action. The loop-blocked Continue now asks Apollo to replan with Atlas evidence (hop, telemetry, recovery, design) instead of spinning on the same hop.

Fluidity: the 5s Parthenon tick is gone, inactive-pane polls are reduced, the brain shows at most 120 high-confidence instincts (archived hidden), and the GPU fallback marker is cleared so hardware acceleration is tried again. Live preview keeps the preview but no longer stops the live campaign server during hibernate.

Hibernation no longer parks a live campaign: a live walk keeps its OpenCode/MCP server and preview; the window sleeps. Window controls render whenever the preload window API exists, with a Linux fallback.
Instincts are technical vs project: completed hops write a global technical/quick-circuit pattern (provenance kept), project facts stay scoped; Callimachus keeps the pool capped and high-signal.
OpenCode v2 2.4.2 is vendored and gate-approved (first run hit a transient v2-session-list 503; the clean retry passed every check).
Notifications: learning/instinct messages are translated in all seven languages.
Six current screenshots (Pantheon, live preview, preview window, cost, logs, phone); README/UX-TOUR trimmed and updated.

releases.title: The stable launch — lane truth, the walk continues, Apollo answers where
highlights: GO lane truth: every lane was probed with a real 1-token turn. deepseek-v4.1-flash, mimo-v2.6-flash, hy3, kimi-k2.7-code and glm-5.3-flash answer OK; qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.8-flash and minimax-m3 answer 'OpenCode Go requires an API key' and are marked auth (never silently retried). A dead lane fails over to the verified GO roster with the cause; raw harness-only refusals can no longer abort a healthy turn.

The walk continues: on a DONE generation the detached walker applies the staged dispatch-plan.next.json and keeps walking (bounded to 8 generations per process). A park never auto-advances. Preflight still adopts artifacts already on disk at zero tokens.

Learning closes the loop: every completed hop writes/updates an empirical instinct (samples + confidence), the gate short-circuits only when both specific tags match, and one quiet 'new instinct' notification is emitted per new pattern. 139 empirical instincts were backfilled from the AIME telemetry.

Apollo reports WHERE / WHAT HAPPENED / NEXT / NEED YOU / FILES from disk before answering; the God panel carries a compact status brief card (project, generation, hops, current hop, park, preview, design provenance).

Preview window uses the browser iframe (the Electron popup no longer renders black). Marks queue durably and batch to Apollo; the per-card chat is Apollo-only and the card opens the latest activity sheet.
Boot handshake accepts Next 16 CSS under static/chunks, so a complete production build no longer shows the repair card or the stacked loaders.
Cost and Smart Burn never spin forever: the ledger is incrementally cached, the dashboards time out at 20s, keep the last good reading, and expose retry + a campaign-aware empty state.

Design truth: the project design-review.json is the score; a dated page review is a separate fallback number with its source. The repair loop keeps the project's floor instead of accepting 7.8 under an 8 gate.
Notifications collapse identical events inside 10 minutes into one row with an honest ×N; the phone sheet and PC center share the same dedupe and palette.
57 hermetic suites green (including the new learning-loop and go-lane-fallback suites). Hygiene: tsc, lint, docs, privacy and audit. Limits are declared in HYGIENE.md, never hidden.

releases.title: Hygiene total — zero errors + the interactive preview and the phone
highlights: Live preview is interactive again: Electron renders a <webview> at the REAL origin (127.0.0.1/LAN), so the project cookies and localStorage survive; the 127.0.0.2 alias (logged-out mirror) is retired.

The hop SSE replay is ignored until stream_ready; a landed part is offered ("part ready · refresh") and auto-follow waits 15s of idle. The probe no longer re-renders on latency jitter. Device presets, fullscreen and a wrapping toolbar cover phone/tablet/PC.

The phone sends x-olympus-language, merges the god text parts (a log can no longer replace the answer), streams the reply, stops on demand, primes audio on the first gesture, auto-enables performance mode on low-end hardware, and its preview sheet reloads/marks a real app.

The pairing card reads a live phone heartbeat (connected · last seen) and a server-lifetime supervisor restarts the desired Cloudflare tunnel after a crash or wake. The LAN origin makes the shell usable from another PC.

Performance: the hop-event JSONL is parsed once per file change per process (shared cache), mobile polling is 10s/20s with state-equality bailouts, and the boot gate caps its data wait at 2.5s and preloads the first frames.
npm run hygiene is the gate of record: tsc, lint, docs, privacy, suite manifest and audit-high all pass; add --battery for the 55 hermetic suites. HYGIENE.md declares every remaining limit.
The 0.0.98 preview releases are retired from Releases (tags kept); v0.0.98 is the base and v0.0.99 is the current stable. No external projects were created; AIME remains the active development lane.

releases.title: The walk waits, recovers and reports — and the Logs tell the truth
highlights: The GO 5-hour limit is now a WAIT, not an unknown stop: provider.go-limit/quota maps to provider-quota, the walk pauses and resumes at the console reset. The old overnight park (21:31 → 06:25) can no longer burn a night.

A blocked design gate recovers its quarantined dependencies (the real QA parks), not the gate. The end-of-walk report is deterministic and always written; the digest now counts the hop state (6/10, not 4/10).
Apollo's chat gets a durable campaign reporter: hop green/parked, quota wait and the final report are in the inbox, so a detached walk still speaks after a reload.

New Logs workspace: Visão geral, Hops, Walks, Models and Economy, with full hop/walk detail — god, build, model, declared abilities, artifacts, checks, park, recovery, resonance, tokens, step cost/list/invoice.

The terminal header now carries the GO limit meter: 5h by default, one button toggles weekly/monthly; stale anchor and quota-hit are labelled. The meter reads the console anchor only (no 57k ledger scan).
Hibernation now opts the active lane in and starts the detached walk, so the night contract survives the renderer being destroyed.
The qwen3.7-plus guard and the exact console windows from v0.0.97 remain. OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and gate-approved.

The task sheet now shows the build's own loadout (skills/MCPs/demigods even when the hop declares none), lane health, live tool counts, the last park/recovery and the settled output tail — no more 0/0 with no explanation.
Learning notifications are live and clickable: the box shows the teaching, measured confidence/samples and exactly how far it is from the 85% short-circuit gate, with the last outcomes.
Callimachus gets a brain-health card (seed/empirical, average confidence, short-circuit rate, the 85% gate) and a 'curar agora' action; his reference shelf now includes the vault knowledge docs.

Pattern Studio: moving the pointer attracts the particle field, clicking the background pulses it, and clicking a thought opens its analysis box (what it is, connections, associated learning) — the learning rows open the same detail.
Boot: one full-screen loader loops until every mounted panel is loadable, instead of a stack of per-panel loaders; the brain's focus card no longer covers the live logo.
The Logs hop detail now shows the output tail and falls back to the frozen plan for historical hop definitions; the hop table is a responsive two-line list with cost visible.

releases.title: The GO console is the anchor — no more stale burn
highlights: The logged-in OpenCode GO console is already an OLYMPUS frame; every 30s it is parsed (monthly / rolling / weekly + reset) and posted as the anchor, source browser. The app graph follows 46% / 100% / 52% with no manual copy.

A console anchor older than 5 minutes PAUSES upgrades. Rolling ≥65% steps down, ≥80% enforces Reserve, and 100% is a quota-hit: the walker parks with the console reset time and Burn/Pace are disabled.
The burn panel shows the console anchor age, the rolling number, the stale/quota banners and the resume time; off/reserve remain available.

The interactive chat now pins the session model to the current god's model every message. The unverified GO qwen3.7-plus lane falls back to verified DeepSeek, so a qwen turn can no longer leave Apollo riding the same dead lane.

Verified live: the console frame auto-synced 46% monthly / 100% rolling / 52% weekly and the quota guard parked the walk; after the rolling window reset the frame reported 0% rolling, then 47% monthly / 1% rolling / 52% weekly as the first post-reset turn landed, and the guard released. The qwen guard maps to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash.
OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and gate-approved.

releases.title: Hibernation v2, GO truth and the smart burn
highlights: X now quits by default; hibernate is explicit (tray, lock, or the close-to-hibernate preference). A real quit stops the preview/MCP fleet instead of leaving it in the app cgroup.
Hibernate waits for a streaming chat turn, keeps a preview only when a live hop needs it, records the servers it stops, and the wake restores them automatically.
The hibernation HUD has a collapse button: 420×720 → 340×190 (campaign, GO month, in-flight hop only); expand restores the full widget.
The GO graph uses the console anchor (monthly/5h/weekly) plus the local delta; the weekly window resets Monday 00:00 UTC. The measured 25.1% / 50.1% matches the console's 25% / on-pace-50%.

Smart burn chooses a GO-only roster at the next hop/message (Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code, DeepSeek 1017, Qwen3.7 Plus, MiniMax M3). Claude Opus/Sonnet are Zen models, not in the GO catalog; the screen says so instead of guessing.
The burn toggle never rewrites opencode.json and never cuts a live turn; it applies at the hop/message boundary and diversifies top lanes so one per-model cap cannot carry all ten gods.
OpenCode v2 2.3.2 remains the latest npm release and is gate-approved; the patch-notes screen checks the live latest on every open.
A tag-icon/logo audit and a 24px vector brief are in docs/design/TAG-ICON-BRIEF.md; the 16px marks are hand-authored, not model-generated.
Wake ignores ERR_ABORTED (the splash → APP_URL navigation) instead of entering a reload loop; the preview restore probes and retries until verified.
Max Quality / strategy apply resolves the real app root in standalone (not .next/standalone); the L4 probe falls back to the package binary. Verified ok:true.

releases.title: OpenCode 2.3.2 alignment and the patch-notes screen
highlights: OpenCode v2 2.3.2 passed the isolated conformance gate (serve, v2 sessions, prompt/SSE, DB schema, tokens, abort) and a real Apollo turn.
The boot loader now shows a What's new card after the first second; a hibernate return repaints the same loader, so the alignment is visible during a slow wake.
A status-bar Patch notes button opens the full updates screen from anywhere; /patch-notes is also a standalone page.
The screen reads the installed and npm-latest OpenCode versions live and takes the tested version from patch-notes.json, so it stays updatable without hardcoding the UI.
The update lane still refuses an ungated version and shows the conformance command instead of updating blind.

releases.title: The preview that obeys, the marks that cannot be lost
highlights: Browser previews keep 127.0.0.1 (the project session survives); Electron alone uses the isolated 127.0.0.2 OOPIF origin for 60 FPS.
Apollo mark batches are durable background plans with plan/latest/retry, a 20-minute budget and boot-aware stale recovery.
The small preview sends to Apollo; every non-quick mark is saved to the project queue before the turn.
Hibernation stops managed dev servers and prunes an expired window; dev servers report RSS, adopt the true port owner and restart in place.
Next.js 16.4.6 closes the advisory that made 16.4.2 fail the build.

releases.title: Performance: the preview gets its own renderer
highlights: Electron runs the live preview as an OOPIF on 127.0.0.2; AIME measured parent 54 → 60 FPS and iframe 52 → 60 FPS.
GPU is on by default; a persisted software-rendering marker was retired.
Progressive boot waits for the shell, not nine panel endpoints; heavy panes show their own branded loaders.
